A1.justification: Both 11-page PDFs describe the same 3D-LLaVA research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and references support reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark results in Table 2, component ablations in Tables 3–5, and qualitative outputs in Figure 5.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark results and ablations and adds original box-level grounding results in Table 3.

M1.justification: The architecture, OST components, training objectives and mask-generation procedure remain unchanged. V2 adds a limited inference adaptation for box grounding: remove mask outliers using DBSCAN, then obtain a bounding box from the remaining points' minimum and maximum coordinates (Section 4.4).

E1.justification: The reported training coverage drops Sr3D, SceneVerse scene-level captions and Grounded 3D-LLM object descriptions (Section 3.4 and Table 1). V2 also adds box-level ScanRefer grounding. These are bounded coverage changes within the retained ScanNet domain and five original evaluation datasets.

E2.justification: V2's new box-grounding comparison includes ConcretNet, which was absent from v1, alongside 3D-VisTA, 3D-LLM, Grounded 3D-LLM and Chat-Scene. Table 2's comparator membership remains unchanged. Random selection and farthest point sampling disappear as comparison variants when the token-selection ablation is removed.

E3.justification: Table 1 substantially revises the reported instruction-tuning recipe from 393K to 295K examples, removing 66K Sr3D examples and 32K additional captions/descriptions while retaining one training epoch. V2 also introduces box-grounding evaluation using DBSCAN-filtered masks and Acc@0.25/Acc@0.5. The PDFs do not establish whether the training-data revision reflects corrected documentation or retraining.

E4.justification: V1's Table 4 and accompanying visual-token-selection analysis are removed, eliminating the ablation comparing objectness-based selection with random selection and farthest point sampling. The prompt-encoding ablation survives as v2 Table 4; token-count sensitivity in Table 5 and qualitative examples in Figure 5 remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added grounding table continues the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 Table 3 adds box-grounding results: 3D-LLaVA obtains 51.2/40.6 at Acc@0.25/Acc@0.5, versus Chat-Scene's 55.5/50.2. V1's token-selection ablation results are removed. Table 2, retained ablation values and Figure 1's existing numerical labels are unchanged; these do not demonstrate a performance gain between versions.

T1.justification: The distance-adaptive attention equation and both training-loss equations, including the 0.1 mask-loss coefficient, are unchanged. Neither version introduces additional theoretical results, formal assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: an integrated generalist 3D LMM, OST's three functions, and strong multi-task performance. The added box-grounding experiment does not redefine the stated main contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds an interpretation contrasting mask optimization with competitors' box-based objectives and acknowledges weaker box-grounding performance than Chat-Scene, while discussing architectural advantages. The token-selection ablation's interpretation is removed. The concluding limitation about insufficient 3D data is retained, moving from v1 page 9 to v2 page 8.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a project repository link on the title page, replacing v1's future-release promise with concrete access information. It also documents DBSCAN filtering and coordinate-based box extraction for the new evaluation. Existing hardware, optimizer, learning-rate and model-configuration details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds the DBSCAN reference by Ester et al. and the work cited for ConcretNet by Unal et al., and removes SceneVerse. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain essentially unchanged; most other reference edits concern numbering and citation back-references.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording and grammar edits, renames Section 4.4 from 'Ablation Study' to 'Experimental Analysis', replaces one analysis subsection and adds acknowledgements. The overall section sequence and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with three additional metric axes, the LEO series, revised styling and a comparability note. Table 1 is shortened, the new grounding table replaces the token-selection display, and the prompt ablation is renumbered. Other figures and the two-column layout remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful box-grounding evidence and acknowledges its performance gap, while providing a repository link and a more complete overview figure. However, it removes the direct token-selection ablation and revises training data from 393K to 295K without clarifying how the unchanged benchmark results relate to that revision. These benefits, lost supporting evidence and unresolved experimental history prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
